title: 🍤 Startup Pitch Battle
description: You've got a brilliant startup idea! But can you convince investors to fund it? Build your pitch deck, face tough investor objections, iterate your product, manage your burn rate, and compete against rival startups. From idea to Series A -- survive the gauntlet!
learning_objectives: Understand the startup lifecycle from ideation to Series A funding
Learn to build and deliver a compelling pitch deck under pressure
Practice financial literacy through burn rate, runway, and valuation concepts
Develop strategic thinking around product-market fit, pivoting, and scaling
Build resilience and decision-making skills in high-stakes entrepreneurial scenarios
Understand term sheets, equity dilution, and investor negotiation dynamics

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: You are a first-time founder entering the Indian startup ecosystem with a big idea
Each round presents a critical startup milestone -- from choosing your idea to negotiating a term sheet
Make strategic decisions that affect your Pitch Score, Product Readiness, Investor Confidence, and more
Manage your Burn Rate and Runway carefully -- run out of months, and your startup dies
Compete against TechNova, an aggressive rival startup trying to beat you to market
Survive all 10 rounds and secure Series A funding to win!
tips: Balance speed and quality -- moving too fast creates a fragile product, but moving too slow lets competitors win
Investor Confidence is the most critical stat for the final VC Pitch Day round
Your Burn Rate increases naturally each round as your team grows -- keep an eye on Runway
Team Strength multiplies the impact of your other decisions -- invest in people early

player_profile.name: First-time Founder
player_profile.background: Student with a startup idea entering the Indian startup ecosystem

competitors.name: TechNova (Rival Startup)
competitors.description: An aggressive, well-funded rival startup founded by IIT Delhi grads. They move fast, break things, and are always one step behind -- or ahead -- of you.

rounds.title: Round 1: The Idea
rounds.story:
Welcome to Bangalore's legendary startup ecosystem! You're sitting in a noisy Third Wave Coffee outlet on Church Street, laptop open, dreaming big.

Your college senior -- now a Y Combinator alum -- just texted you: "India's startup scene is on fire. Pick a sector and build something real. I'll intro you to angels if you're serious."

Your Pitch Score is {{pitch_score}} and you have {{runway_months}} months of runway. Four sectors are calling your name. Each has a different risk-reward profile in the Indian market.

What kind of startup will you build?
rounds.goal: Choose your startup sector and define your vision
rounds.setting: Third Wave Coffee, Church Street, Bangalore

npc_dialogue.text: Listen yaar, India has 800 million smartphone users and half the population is under 25. Pick something that solves a REAL problem, not some Silicon Valley copycat. The market will reward authenticity.

choices.label: 📚 EdTech -- AI Tutoring Platform
choices.description: Build an AI-powered tutoring platform for students preparing for JEE, NEET, and board exams. Massive market (300M+ students), proven demand, but intense competition from Byju's, Unacademy, and PhysicsWallah. Moderate risk.
choices.feedback: 📚 Smart choice! EdTech is a proven market in India. Investors know the TAM is massive. But you'll need a killer differentiator to stand out from the giants. Your Y Combinator friend replies: "EdTech? Good. Focus on Tier 2/3 cities -- that's where the real growth is."

choices.label: 💳 FinTech -- UPI Savings App for Gen Z
choices.description: Create a micro-savings and investment app built on UPI for teenagers and young adults. Unique angle in India's digital payments revolution. RBI regulations are complex but the opportunity is enormous. Higher risk, higher reward.
choices.feedback: 💳 Bold move! FinTech is where the big money flows in India. UPI has transformed payments. But RBI compliance will eat up time and money. Your friend warns: "FinTech = high ceiling, but regulatory landmines everywhere. Get a compliance person on Day 1."

choices.label: 🏥 HealthTech -- Rural Telemedicine
choices.description: Build a telemedicine platform connecting rural India with urban doctors. India has 1 doctor per 1,500 people in villages. Huge social impact, government support possible, but slow monetization and infrastructure challenges.
choices.feedback: 🏥 A startup with purpose! Rural telemedicine is a genuine need. Investors are increasingly interested in impact-driven startups. But monetization will be tricky -- rural users can't pay premium prices. Your friend says: "Health + impact = great story for investors. But prove unit economics early."

choices.label: 🌾 AgriTech -- Farm-to-Table Supply Chain
choices.description: Disrupt India's broken agricultural supply chain. Connect farmers directly to restaurants and retailers using an app. 60% of India depends on agriculture. Massive market but deeply entrenched middlemen and logistics nightmares.
choices.feedback: 🌾 The hard path! AgriTech is a trillion-dollar market that has defeated many startups. The supply chain is broken but fixing it requires ground-level operations. Your friend's honest take: "AgriTech is where dreamers go to suffer... but the ones who survive build empires. DeHaat raised $115M. It's possible."

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling Third Wave Coffee outlet on Church Street, vibrant with colorful decor, laptops open on tables, coffee cups steaming, and baristas working, filled with aspiring entrepreneurs
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What tradeoff did this decision reveal? What did you gain, and what did you give up?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 2: Building the Team
rounds.story:
Your idea is taking shape! But you can't do this alone.

You're at the HSR Layout co-working space, and three potential co-founders have expressed interest. Meanwhile, you need to decide your hiring strategy for the first 2-3 employees.

Your burn rate is ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month and you have {{runway_months}} months of runway. Every hire increases your burn rate but also your capability.

💬 Your mentor from IIM Bangalore calls:

npc_dialogue.text: The number one reason startups fail isn't the idea -- it's the team. Choose a co-founder who complements your weaknesses, not someone who thinks exactly like you. And remember, equity split decisions made today will haunt or help you for years.
I can build the tech, but I want 30% equity and full control over the engineering roadmap. I've seen too many startups where the business side micromanages the tech side. Non-negotiable.

choices.label: 👨‍💻 Hire Vikram as CTO (30% equity)
choices.description: Bring on Vikram, the IIT Bombay engineer, as co-founder and CTO with 30% equity. He's brilliant but opinionated. Gives you a strong tech foundation and credibility with investors. Burns rate increases as you hire 2 junior devs under him.
choices.feedback: Vikram joins as CTO! His IIT pedigree immediately impresses the investor community. He hires two junior devs from his college network. Your product velocity triples overnight. But your burn rate just jumped significantly -- ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month is no joke. Vikram's first Slack message to the team: "Ship fast or ship out. We're building something real."

choices.label: 💼 Hire Neha as COO (25% equity)
choices.description: Bring on Neha, a former Flipkart operations manager, as co-founder and COO with 25% equity. She knows the Indian market inside out and has investor connections. You'll outsource tech development to a freelance team in Hyderabad.
choices.feedback: Neha's Flipkart experience is gold! She immediately creates a business plan, identifies your first 50 potential customers, and sets up meetings with three angel investors. Product development is slower with freelancers, but your pitch deck looks razor-sharp. Neha's mantra: "Don't build it until someone will pay for it."

choices.label: 💪 Go Solo -- Hire Freelancers Only
choices.description: Keep 100% equity. Hire freelance developers and a part-time marketing person. You maintain full control but carry all the weight. Investors typically prefer teams over solo founders.
choices.feedback: You're going solo! Maximum equity retention but maximum stress. Late nights coding, early mornings pitching, and nobody to share the burden. Your mentor Priya frowns: "Solo founders have a 3x higher failure rate. Investors want to see a team, not a hero." The burn rate is low though -- you're lean and mean.

choices.label: 🌟 Hire Both + Intern Army (Split equity)
choices.description: Bring on Vikram (20% equity) AND Neha (15% equity) plus recruit 3 college interns. A full team from Day 1. Maximum firepower but your burn rate will skyrocket and runway shrinks dangerously.
choices.feedback: Full team assembled! You've got engineering, operations, and hungry interns. The energy in your co-working space is electric. But with ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month burn rate and only {{runway_months}} months of runway, you're in a race against the clock. Vikram and Neha clash immediately over priorities. Welcome to startup co-founder dynamics!

rounds.image_prompt: a bright co-working space filled with colorful desks and lively discussions, sunlight streaming through large windows, a group of diverse individuals engaged in animated conversation around a table
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 3: MVP Development
rounds.story:
It's 2 AM at your HSR Layout flat. Pizza boxes are stacked in the corner. Your team has been coding for 3 weeks straight.

The question that's tearing your team apart: Do you ship a rough MVP NOW and get real user feedback? Or take 2 more months to build something polished?

Product Readiness: {{product_readiness}}%
Burn Rate: ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month
Runway: {{runway_months}} months

TechNova, your rival, just posted on LinkedIn that their beta is launching next week.
rounds.setting: Late-night coding session, HSR Layout flat, Bangalore

npc_dialogue.text: The code is held together with duct tape and prayers. If we ship now, it WILL crash for the first 100 users. But we'll learn what they actually want. Ship or sink?
Excited to announce TechNova's beta launch next week! 500 users already on the waitlist. The future of [your sector] starts now. 🚀 #StartupLife #Disruption

choices.label: 🚀 Ship Now -- Move Fast, Break Things
choices.description: Launch a rough but functional MVP this week. It'll crash, it'll have bugs, but you'll get real user data. Speed beats perfection in startup world. Reid Hoffman said, "If you're not embarrassed by your first product, you shipped too late."
choices.feedback: 🚀 MVP shipped! It crashes twice on Day 1, the login screen has a typo, and one user's data gets lost. But 73 people sign up in the first week and you get 200+ feedback messages. The data is GOLD. You now know exactly what to build next. Your first user review: "Buggy but brilliant. Fix the crashes and I'll pay for this." TechNova notices your launch and panics internally.

choices.label: 🛠️ Take 2 More Months -- Build It Right
choices.description: Invest 2 more months in building a polished, stable product. Better UX, no crashes, proper data security. You'll launch behind TechNova but with a superior product. Costs more runway but makes a stronger first impression.
choices.feedback: 🛠️ Two months of heads-down building. The product looks BEAUTIFUL. Smooth onboarding, zero crashes, clean design. But you burned through ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month for 2 extra months while TechNova grabbed early users. When you finally launch, users love the polish. But your runway is dangerously short at {{runway_months}} months. Was perfection worth it?

choices.label: 🔄 Split the Team -- Ship Core + Build Features
choices.description: Half the team ships a bare-bones core feature NOW. The other half keeps building the full product. You launch something, but the team is stretched thin and nobody's doing their best work.
choices.feedback: 🔄 Compromise achieved! The core feature launches and gets decent traction (45 signups). Meanwhile, the full product is taking shape. But your team is exhausted and morale is dropping. Vikram snaps at an intern at 3 AM. Two team members call in sick the same day. The startup grind is real -- and you're learning that splitting focus is the silent startup killer.

choices.label: 💡 Pivot -- Launch a Simpler Version First
choices.description: Scrap the original plan. Build something 10x simpler that solves ONE core problem brilliantly. A landing page + WhatsApp bot instead of a full app. Validates demand with almost no code.
choices.feedback: 💡 Genius move! You launch a WhatsApp bot + simple landing page in 3 days. Cost: almost nothing. Result: 200 people interact with the bot in the first week, and you collect incredible data about what they actually need. An angel investor sees your landing page and DMs you: "I love the scrappy approach. Let's talk." Sometimes the smartest tech decision is to use less tech.

rounds.image_prompt: a cluttered living room at 2 AM, pizza boxes piled high, laptops open with lines of code on screens, team members in deep discussion, dim light casting shadows on the walls
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this option? What were you trying to protect or grow?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 4: First Customer Demo
rounds.story:
DEMO DAY! Your first real potential customer -- a mid-size company -- is visiting your cramped office (okay, it's still your flat, but you rearranged the furniture).

The customer is Ramesh Iyer, procurement head at a respected firm. He's seen 12 pitches this month and looks tired. You have exactly 20 minutes.

Halfway through your demo, the app crashes. The screen freezes. Ramesh raises an eyebrow.

Product Readiness: {{product_readiness}}%
Pitch Score: {{pitch_score}}

🚨 CRISIS MOMENT: Your demo just crashed in front of the customer!
rounds.goal: Handle the demo crash and win your first customer
rounds.setting: Your startup flat converted into a makeshift office, Koramangala, Bangalore

npc_dialogue.text: Look, I've seen a lot of startups. The ones that succeed aren't the ones with perfect products -- they're the ones who handle problems honestly. Your app just crashed. What are you going to do about it?
The backup server is working. I can get it running again in 5 minutes. Or we can switch to the slide deck. Your call, founder.

choices.label: 😅 Own It -- Be Brutally Honest
choices.description: Laugh at the crash, admit you're an early-stage startup, and use the downtime to have a genuine conversation with Ramesh about his actual pain points. Vulnerability builds trust.
choices.feedback: 😅 You laugh and say, "Well, that's startup life! Let me tell you what we're ACTUALLY building while my co-founder fixes this." Ramesh laughs for the first time. You spend 15 minutes in genuine conversation about his problems. He reveals pain points you never knew existed. By the end, he says: "I like your honesty. Send me a proposal. I'll give you a 3-month pilot -- but fix that crash." FIRST CUSTOMER ACQUIRED! 🎉

choices.label: 📊 Switch to Slide Deck -- Keep It Professional
choices.description: Smoothly transition to your polished slide deck while the app reboots. Show market data, competitor analysis, and your roadmap. Professional but less authentic. Ramesh has seen a hundred slide decks.
choices.feedback: 📊 Smooth recovery! You seamlessly pull up the slide deck and deliver a polished presentation. Ramesh nods politely. When the app finally reboots, you show a quick demo. His response: "Nice deck. Let me think about it." That's corporate speak for 'maybe.' You follow up three times over two weeks. Eventually he agrees to a small trial, but at a discounted rate. Professional, but you missed the chance to build a real connection.

choices.label: 📝 Whiteboard Session -- Co-create the Solution
choices.description: Grab a marker, go to the whiteboard, and ask Ramesh to help you design the perfect solution for his company. Turn a failed demo into a collaborative design session. Risky but potentially transformative.
choices.feedback: 📝 BRILLIANT PIVOT! Ramesh's eyes light up when you hand him the marker. For 30 minutes, he draws out exactly what his company needs. You take furious notes. By the end, he's essentially designed your product roadmap for you -- for free! He says: "This is MY solution now. I want to be your first customer AND your design partner. Let's do a 6-month contract." You just turned a disaster into your biggest win. 🌟

choices.label: ⏰ Blame the Wi-Fi -- Reschedule for Next Week
choices.description: Make an excuse about internet issues, apologize profusely, and ask to reschedule. Gives you time to fix bugs but Ramesh might not come back. He's a busy person with other options.
choices.feedback: ⏰ Ramesh sighs. He's heard the Wi-Fi excuse from four other startups. "Sure, let's reschedule," he says flatly. Your co-founder texts you after: "He's not coming back." Two weeks later, you email Ramesh. No response. Three weeks later, you see his LinkedIn post: "Excited to partner with TechNova for our digital transformation!" 💩 You lost the customer AND gave them to your rival.

rounds.image_prompt: a small, cluttered office with makeshift furniture and an anxious atmosphere, a laptop displaying a frozen screen, a weary man in a suit looking surprised at the demo failure, warm lighting
rounds.coaching_moment: Look at your current resource levels — which constraint are you trying to address?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 5: Angel Investor Meeting
rounds.story:
THE MOMENT OF TRUTH. You've scored a meeting with Kavitha Reddy, one of Bangalore's most respected angel investors. She's backed 15 startups, 3 became unicorns.

You're in the elevator of UB City mall. Kavitha steps in. She's heading to the same floor.

"You're that startup I've been hearing about," she says. "You have until we reach the 12th floor. Go."

Pitch Score: {{pitch_score}}
Investor Confidence: {{investor_confidence}}%
Runway: {{runway_months}} months

⏰ You have 60 seconds. This is your elevator pitch.
rounds.goal: Deliver a compelling elevator pitch to an angel investor

npc_dialogue.text: I hear 50 pitches a month. Most founders talk about their product. The ones I fund talk about the problem, the customer, and the numbers. I don't invest in technology -- I invest in founders who understand their market. 12th floor. Go.

choices.label: 🚨 Lead with the Problem -- Data-Driven Pitch
choices.description: Start with a shocking statistic about the problem you're solving. "Did you know that [X million] Indians face [problem] every day?" Follow with your solution, traction, and ask. Classic investor pitch framework.
choices.feedback: 🚨 Kavitha's eyes widen at your opening statistic. She asks two sharp follow-up questions. By the 12th floor, she's scribbling your name in her phone. "Come to my office Thursday. Bring your financials and your co-founder. I want to hear more." As the elevator opens, she adds: "I like you. You led with the customer, not the tech. That tells me you understand what matters." Thursday's meeting goes brilliantly. She offers ₹25 lakh in angel funding!

choices.label: 📈 Lead with Traction -- Show the Numbers
choices.description: Open with your best metrics: users, revenue, growth rate. "We launched 6 weeks ago. Here are our numbers." Investors love traction over talk. Let the data speak.
choices.feedback: 📈 Numbers don't lie! Kavitha nods approvingly as you rattle off growth metrics. "Week-over-week growth of 15%? That's solid for this stage," she says. She asks about unit economics and customer acquisition cost. You stumble slightly on CAC but recover. "You're early but the trajectory is right. Email me a one-pager and let's schedule a proper meeting." She invests ₹15 lakh -- smaller check but with a promise to follow on if you hit milestones.

choices.label: ❤️ Lead with Your Story -- Emotional Connection
choices.description: Share the personal experience that inspired your startup. "Let me tell you why I'm building this..." Connect emotionally before diving into business details. People invest in people.
choices.feedback: ❤️ Kavitha's expression softens as you share your personal story. She can tell this isn't just a business for you -- it's a mission. "I believe in you," she says. "But belief doesn't close deals. Send me the numbers by Friday. If the financials work, I'm in." Your story bought you a warm connection. Now you need to back it up with data. She eventually invests ₹10 lakh -- small but comes with invaluable mentorship and introductions to 3 VC firms.

choices.label: 📱 Pull Out Your Phone -- Live Demo in the Elevator
choices.description: Skip the words. Open your app on your phone and hand it to Kavitha. "Try it. 30 seconds. Tell me what you think." High risk -- if it works, it's unforgettable. If it crashes...
choices.feedback: 📱 Bold move! Kavitha takes your phone, taps around for 20 seconds... and the app loads slowly on the elevator's weak signal. She sees the core functionality but the experience is laggy. "Interesting product. But I need more than a demo -- I need to understand the business." She hands back your phone. "Send me a deck." Not a rejection, but not the slam-dunk you hoped for. Lesson learned: investors invest in businesses, not just products. She passes for now.

rounds.image_prompt: a sleek elevator interior with polished metal and glass, dim ambient lighting creating a tense atmosphere, a digital display showing the ascending floor number, urgency in the air
rounds.coaching_moment: Sometimes the bold choice carries risk, but also the highest reward. Weigh carefully.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How might the people affected by this choice experience the outcome?

expert_pick.reason: Calculated risk-taking is what separates growth-oriented leaders from status-quo managers.

rounds.title: Round 6: Competitor Threat
rounds.story:
🚨 RED ALERT 🚨

You wake up to 47 WhatsApp messages and a trending Twitter thread.

TechNova just launched a product almost IDENTICAL to yours -- with better UI, a celebrity endorsement from a Shark Tank India judge, and ₹2 crore in fresh funding.

Their launch video has 500K views. Your team is panicking. Two of your users just switched to TechNova. Your intern is updating his LinkedIn.

Team Strength: {{team_strength}}%
Investor Confidence: {{investor_confidence}}%
Runway: {{runway_months}} months

💬 Your co-founder sends a voice note at 6 AM:
rounds.goal: Respond strategically to a major competitor threat
rounds.setting: Early morning crisis, your Bangalore flat

npc_dialogue.text: Have you SEEN TechNova's launch? It's everywhere! Our users are DMing me asking if we're shutting down. The intern just asked if he should update his resume. We need to DO something. Today.

Thrilled to launch TechNova 2.0! Thanks to @SharkTankIndia's Aman Gupta for believing in our vision. We're here to disrupt. If you're building something similar... maybe it's time to consider joining us? 😏 #TechNovaLaunch
I saw TechNova's launch. Don't panic. Competition validates the market. The question is: what can you do that they can't? Call me tonight -- let's strategize.

choices.label: 🎯 Double Down on Differentiation
choices.description: Study TechNova's product obsessively, identify their weaknesses, and build features they can't replicate. Go deeper into your niche. Be the specialist while they try to be everything. Takes time but builds a defensible moat.
choices.feedback: 🎯 Smart strategy! You spend a week dissecting TechNova's product and find three critical gaps. They optimized for flashy features but missed the core user need. You build a feature so good that users start switching BACK from TechNova. One user tweets: "Tried TechNova. Looks pretty but doesn't actually solve my problem. Going back to [your startup]." Kavitha texts: "Now THAT'S how you compete. Keep going." 💪

choices.label: 🤝 Approach TechNova -- Propose Partnership
choices.description: Reach out to TechNova's CEO. Propose a strategic partnership or API integration. If you can't beat them, work with them. Controversial but pragmatic. Your team might see it as surrender.
choices.feedback: 🤝 You DM TechNova's CEO. Surprisingly, he responds: "Interesting. Let's talk." But the meeting reveals he wants to ACQUIRE you for a low price, not partner as equals. He offers ₹50 lakh -- barely covering your costs. Your team is demoralized. Vikram says: "We didn't start a company to work for someone else." You walk away from the deal but learned a valuable lesson: never negotiate from weakness. The silver lining? You now know their strategy from the inside.

choices.label: 🚀 Speed Blitz -- Launch 3 Features in 2 Weeks
choices.description: Go into war mode. No sleep, no weekends. Ship three major features in two weeks to show users you're faster and more innovative. Burn bright and fast. Risk burning out your team entirely.
choices.feedback: 🚀 WAR MODE ACTIVATED! Your team pulls 18-hour days for two weeks straight. You ship three features that TechNova hasn't even announced. Users are impressed. Tech blogs notice. YourStory writes: "Scrappy underdog takes on well-funded TechNova." But the cost is severe: your designer quits from burnout, Vikram hasn't slept in 3 days, and two features have bugs you haven't fixed. You won the battle but might be losing the war. Runway: {{runway_months}} months.

choices.label: 🧘 Ignore TechNova -- Focus on Customers
choices.description: Stop checking TechNova's Twitter. Instead, call every single one of your users personally. Ask what they need. Build THAT. Let the competitor fight for headlines while you fight for customers.
choices.feedback: 🧘 You call all 87 of your users over the weekend. Thirty-seven actually pick up. Their feedback is transformative -- you discover a use case you never considered that users LOVE. You build for THEM, not against TechNova. A month later, your NPS score is 72 (TechNova's is 31). Your users become your evangelists. Kavitha says: "This is the founder I invested in. Customer obsession beats competitor obsession every time."

rounds.image_prompt: a dimly lit startup office at dawn, cluttered with coffee cups and laptops, a team huddled around a glowing screen, expressions of concern as messages flood in, urgency in the air
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Looking back, do you think this was the best use of your resources?

expert_pick.reason: Calculated risk-taking is what separates growth-oriented leaders from status-quo managers.

rounds.title: Round 7: Scaling Decisions
rounds.story:
Something incredible is happening. Your user base just crossed 5,000 and is growing 20% week-over-week. Revenue is trickling in. For the first time, people you don't know are using your product.

But growth brings problems. Your server crashed twice last week. Customer support tickets are piling up (you're answering them yourself at midnight). And you just got an email from an enterprise client wanting to deploy your solution across 50 offices.

Burn Rate: ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month
Runway: {{runway_months}} months
Product Readiness: {{product_readiness}}%

💬 Your investor calls with a warning:
rounds.goal: Choose between aggressive growth and sustainable scaling
rounds.setting: Your startup office (you finally got a real one!), Indiranagar, Bangalore

npc_dialogue.text: Growth is oxygen for startups, but growing too fast is the #2 startup killer after running out of cash. You need to decide: are you optimizing for growth or unit economics? Both is not an option right now.

Dear Founder, We'd like to deploy your solution across our 50 offices. Budget: ₹40 lakh/year. But we need enterprise-grade security, 99.9% uptime SLA, and dedicated support. Can you deliver by Q2? -- Regards, Suresh Nair, CTO, MegaCorp India

choices.label: 🏢 Chase Enterprise -- Lock In the Big Client
choices.description: Drop everything and build enterprise features for MegaCorp. ₹40 lakh/year is life-changing revenue. But enterprise sales means long cycles, heavy customization, and you might lose focus on your core product.
choices.feedback: 🏢 You go all-in on enterprise! Two months of painful customization later, MegaCorp signs the contract. ₹40 lakh/year hits your bank account. Your runway extends significantly. But your core product has stagnated. Regular users complain about neglect. TechNova grabs 2,000 of your SMB users while you were building for one big client. Kavitha warns: "Enterprise revenue is addictive but dangerous. Don't become a services company."

choices.label: 🌱 Organic Growth -- Fix Infrastructure First
choices.description: Focus on fixing server stability, reducing bugs, and improving the core product. Let growth happen naturally through word-of-mouth. Decline the enterprise deal for now. Sustainable but slower.
choices.feedback: 🌱 You politely tell MegaCorp, "We're not ready yet. Give us 6 months." Your team breathes a sigh of relief and focuses on making the product bulletproof. Server uptime hits 99.8%. User satisfaction soars. Growth slows to 12% week-over-week but retention jumps to 85%. Your co-founder smiles: "For the first time, I'm not afraid the product will break." MegaCorp respects your honesty and keeps you on their radar.

choices.label: 💰 Raise a Bridge Round -- Get More Capital First
choices.description: Before scaling, raise a small bridge round (₹50 lakh - ₹1 crore) from existing investors and new angels. More money = more runway to do both growth and infrastructure. But equity dilution hits hard at this stage.
choices.feedback: 💰 Kavitha introduces you to two more angel investors. After three weeks of pitching, you close a ₹75 lakh bridge round. Your runway extends by 3 months! But the valuation is lower than you wanted, and you've given up 12% more equity. Your ownership is shrinking. Kavitha reassures: "Better to own 60% of something big than 100% of something dead." With fresh capital, you hire a DevOps engineer and start enterprise prep simultaneously.

choices.label: 👥 Hiring Spree -- Build the Dream Team NOW
choices.description: Hire aggressively: 5 engineers, 2 salespeople, 1 customer success manager. Build the team that can handle both growth and enterprise. Burn rate explodes but capability multiplies.
choices.feedback: 👥 You go on a hiring spree! Eight new faces join in three weeks. Your office is buzzing with energy. But onboarding takes time -- for the first month, productivity actually DROPS as veterans train newbies. Your burn rate skyrockets to ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month. Runway: {{runway_months}} months. Kavitha calls, concerned: "You're burning cash like it's Diwali. Every hire should have clear ROI. Do you have a hiring plan or are you panic-hiring?" Tough question.

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling startup office filled with busy employees at desks stacked with papers, screens displaying growth charts, a large whiteboard covered in ideas, stressed energy in the air
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is this decision optimizing for short-term or long-term outcomes? Which matters more here?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 8: Media Attention
rounds.story:
YOUR STARTUP JUST WENT VIRAL! 📱

A popular tech YouTuber with 3 million subscribers used your product on a livestream and said: "This is genuinely brilliant. Why haven't I heard of this before?"

Overnight: 15,000 new signups. Your servers are groaning. #YourStartup is trending on Twitter India. Three journalists want interviews. A Shark Tank India producer DMs you on Instagram.

But there's a catch -- an angry user also went viral with a complaint thread: "This startup lost my data and won't respond to support tickets."

Pitch Score: {{pitch_score}}
Product Readiness: {{product_readiness}}%

You have 24 hours to decide how to handle this explosion of attention.
rounds.goal: Navigate the double-edged sword of sudden media attention
rounds.setting: Your startup office, phones ringing nonstop

npc_dialogue.text: Chat, look at this. I found this random Indian startup and it actually WORKS. Like, this solves a real problem. @founder if you're watching -- hit me up, I want to feature you on my channel!
THREAD: Why @YourStartup is ALL HYPE. 1) Lost my data. 2) No customer support for 5 days. 3) Charged my card twice. 4) CEO left me on read. AVOID. (1/7) 🧵👇
Hey! Loved what I saw about your startup. We're scouting for Season 4 of Shark Tank India. Would you be interested in pitching? The filming is in 3 weeks. Reply ASAP -- spots fill fast!

choices.label: 🛡️ Address the Angry User First -- Damage Control
choices.description: Before doing ANYTHING else, publicly respond to the angry user thread. Fix their data issue, refund the charges, and post a transparent apology. Handle the fire before chasing the spotlight. Users are watching how you treat complaints.
choices.feedback: 🛡️ You drop everything and write a public response: "@PriyankaTech, you're right. We messed up. Here's what we're doing to fix it: [1] Your data is recovered. [2] Full refund processed. [3] We're hiring a support lead this week. I'm sorry." The tweet gets 50K likes. Users flood the replies: "THIS is how a startup should respond." Priyanka updates her thread: "Update: They actually fixed everything. Respect." Your reputation SOARS. The YouTuber shares your response: "See? This is why I backed them." Crisis turned into PR gold. 🌟

choices.label: 🦈 Say YES to Shark Tank India -- Go Big
choices.description: Accept the Shark Tank India invitation immediately. Spend the next 3 weeks preparing an unforgettable pitch for national TV. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The angry user thread? It'll blow over.
choices.feedback: 🦈 You say YES to Shark Tank! For three weeks, you practice your pitch obsessively. Filming day arrives -- the lights, the cameras, the Sharks. Your pitch is ELECTRIC. Aman Gupta leans forward: "I love this." Namita Thapar asks tough questions you nail perfectly. But while you were preparing, the angry user thread snowballed into a mini-scandal. Product bugs piled up. Two team members felt abandoned. You might get an offer from a Shark, but at what cost to your actual business?

choices.label: 📱 Launch a Content Blitz -- Ride the Wave
choices.description: Strike while the iron is hot! Create content everywhere: LinkedIn posts, a YouTube response video, Twitter threads about your journey. Feed the algorithm. The angry user gets a private DM and resolution. Maximize the viral moment.
choices.feedback: 📱 Content machine activated! You post your founding story on LinkedIn (goes viral: 200K views). You create a YouTube response video thanking the YouTuber. You write a Twitter thread: "From a flat in Koramangala to 15K users: our startup journey." The internet loves an underdog story. Three VCs slide into your DMs. But the angry user notices they got a quiet DM while everyone else got public engagement. She posts: "Funny how they have time for PR but not for customer support." Ouch. Mixed results.

choices.label: 🛠️ Ignore Media -- Stabilize the Product
choices.description: 15,000 new users are about to discover all your product's bugs. Ignore every media request. Fix the product. Scale the servers. Respond to every support ticket. The media will come back if the product is good.
choices.feedback: 🛠️ While TechNova would have jumped on the media attention, you go dark and fix everything. Server capacity tripled. Every support ticket answered within 2 hours. Bug fixes shipped daily. The angry user gets a personal call from you. Of the 15,000 new signups, 11,000 become active users (73% retention -- incredible for a startup). The YouTuber notices: "I recommended this app a week ago and it's actually gotten BETTER since then. That never happens." Slow burn, but powerful.

rounds.title: Round 9: VC Pitch Day
rounds.story:
🎬 THE BIG DAY HAS ARRIVED.

You're standing backstage at the T-Hub in Hyderabad, the largest startup incubator in India. In 15 minutes, you'll pitch to a panel of 5 top VCs for Series A funding.

The stakes: ₹5-10 crore investment. Enough to scale nationally. Enough to crush TechNova. Enough to change your life forever.

The panel includes partners from Sequoia India, Accel, and Blume Ventures. They've funded Zomato, Razorpay, and Cred.

Pitch Score: {{pitch_score}}
Investor Confidence: {{investor_confidence}}%
Product Readiness: {{product_readiness}}%
Team Strength: {{team_strength}}%
Runway: {{runway_months}} months

Your hands are shaking. This is it.
rounds.goal: Deliver the pitch of your life to secure Series A funding

npc_dialogue.text: Welcome to Demo Day! Our next founder has gone from a flat in Koramangala to [user count] users in under a year. Please welcome the founder of [Your Startup]!
We see hundreds of startups. What makes you different isn't your product -- it's your ability to execute. Show me you can build a ₹100 crore business in 5 years. Show me the path.
Your competitor TechNova pitched to us last week. They have more funding and a bigger team. Why should we bet on you instead?
You've got this. Remember -- they're looking for a founder who can navigate chaos and still execute. That's YOU. Breathe.

choices.label: 📊 Data + Storytelling -- The Complete Package
choices.description: Open with your most powerful customer story, then seamlessly transition to metrics, market size, competitive moat, and a clear ask. 12 slides, perfectly rehearsed, mixing emotion with data. The gold standard of VC pitches.
choices.feedback: 📊 MASTERCLASS PITCH! You open with the story of your first customer, Ramesh, and how your product changed his business. The room leans in. Then you hit them with the numbers: growth rate, unit economics, TAM. Slide after slide, perfectly timed. The Sequoia partner stops taking notes and starts nodding. The Accel partner smiles. When you finish, there's a moment of silence. Then: "How much are you raising, and what's the valuation?" THEY WANT IN. Multiple VCs express interest. You're in the driver's seat for the first time. 🚀

choices.label: 💻 Live Demo on Stage -- Show, Don't Tell
choices.description: Ditch most slides. Do a live product demo on the big screen. Show real user data, real transactions, real impact. If it works, it's incredibly powerful. If it crashes on stage... career-ending embarrassment.
choices.feedback: 💻 Heartbeat moment! The screen flickers... and your app loads perfectly. You walk the VCs through a real customer workflow in real-time. The audience watches actual data flowing. It's mesmerizing. One small glitch on the payment screen, but you handle it smoothly: "That's a known issue we're fixing next sprint." The Blume Ventures partner says: "That took guts. I respect founders who let their product speak." You get 2 interested VCs. Not the blowout you hoped for, but solid interest.

choices.label: 🌙 The Moonshot Vision -- Think Massive
choices.description: Paint the picture of a ₹1,000 crore company. Talk about expanding to Southeast Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Show the 10-year roadmap. VCs want to invest in category-defining companies, not small businesses. Dream BIG on stage.
choices.feedback: 🌙 You paint a MASSIVE vision. Global expansion. Platform play. "We're not building an app -- we're building the infrastructure for [sector] across emerging markets." The Sequoia partner's eyes light up -- they love big bets. But the Accel partner pushes back: "That's a great 10-year vision. But what about the next 12 months? What's your path to ₹1 crore MRR?" You stumble slightly on near-term specifics. Mixed response -- one VC loves the ambition, another wants more grounded metrics. You get 1 strong lead and 1 warm interest.

choices.label: 🎬 The Underdog Narrative -- David vs Goliath
choices.description: Lean into your underdog story. Talk about coding from a flat, the demo that crashed, the competitor who tried to crush you. Make the VCs root for you emotionally. Emphasize resilience and scrappiness over polish.
choices.feedback: 🎬 The room is MOVED. You tell the story of the demo crash with Ramesh, the sleepless nights when TechNova launched, the angry user thread you turned into a PR win. People in the audience are tearing up. The Blume Ventures partner says: "I invest in founders, and you're clearly a fighter." But the Sequoia partner wants more rigor: "Great story, but where are the unit economics?" You get warm interest from 2 VCs, but both want to see more data before committing. The emotional pitch opened doors; now you need to close with numbers.

rounds.title: Round 10: Term Sheet Negotiation
rounds.story:
🎉 THEY WANT TO INVEST!

Two VCs have sent term sheets. This is the moment every founder dreams of -- and the moment where the wrong decision can haunt you for a decade.

You're sitting in your lawyer's cramped office on MG Road, staring at two documents that will define the future of your company.

Pitch Score: {{pitch_score}}
Investor Confidence: {{investor_confidence}}%
Burn Rate: ₹{{burn_rate}}K/month
Runway: {{runway_months}} months

💬 Your lawyer and mentor weigh in:
rounds.goal: Navigate term sheet negotiation and close your Series A

npc_dialogue.text: I've seen 200 term sheets in my career. The valuation number is what founders obsess over, but the TERMS are what matter. Liquidation preferences, anti-dilution clauses, board seats -- these clauses can make a ₹10 crore raise feel like a ₹2 crore raise. Read. Every. Word.

Two offers is a great position. But don't get greedy or take too long -- VCs talk to each other, and term sheets have expiry dates. Choose the partner who'll help you when things go wrong, not just when things go right.
I want to make sure the employee stock option pool (ESOP) is large enough. Our engineers need upside. If the ESOP pool is too small, I'll lose my best people to Google and Microsoft within a year.

choices.label: 💰 Accept Offer A: High Valuation (₹40 Cr pre-money)
choices.description: VC firm Pinnacle Capital offers ₹8 crore at ₹40 crore pre-money valuation (16.7% dilution). Great valuation! But: 2x liquidation preference, they want a board seat with veto power on future fundraising, and the ESOP pool is only 5%. They're known for being hands-off until things go wrong -- then they replace founders.
choices.feedback: 💰 You signed with Pinnacle Capital! The headlines look great: "₹40 Crore Valuation!" Twitter celebrates. But your lawyer sighs. The 2x liquidation preference means in any exit under ₹80 crore, the VCs get paid before you. The small ESOP pool frustrates your team. Vikram is unhappy: "My equity is getting diluted to nothing." And the board veto power means Pinnacle can block your next fundraise if they disagree with your direction. High valuation, tough terms. The golden handcuffs are on. Welcome to the big leagues.

choices.label: 🤝 Accept Offer B: Founder-Friendly (₹25 Cr pre-money)
choices.description: Blume Ventures offers ₹5 crore at ₹25 crore pre-money (16.7% dilution). Lower valuation but: 1x liquidation preference (standard), no board veto powers, 15% ESOP pool, and the partner is a former founder who's actively helpful. They're known for being the best board members in India's ecosystem.
choices.feedback: 🤝 You signed with Blume Ventures! The valuation is lower, and you'll see some snarky tweets: "Only ₹25 Cr? TechNova raised at ₹60 Cr." But your lawyer beams: "These are the cleanest terms I've seen this year." The 15% ESOP pool makes your team ecstatic. Vikram gets the equity he wanted. The Blume partner becomes a true mentor -- she introduces you to 10 potential customers and 3 future hires in the first month. Kavitha says: "Smart choice. In 5 years, you'll thank me for pushing you toward founder-friendly terms." This is how empires are built. 🌟

choices.label: 🎲 Play Them Against Each Other -- Counter-offer Both
choices.description: Use the competing offers as leverage. Go back to Pinnacle asking for founder-friendly terms at their valuation. Go back to Blume asking for a higher check size. Classic negotiation tactic but risky -- VCs hate being played against each other, and word travels fast in Bangalore's tight-knit VC community.
choices.feedback: 🎲 Dangerous game! You tell Pinnacle about Blume's terms. You tell Blume about Pinnacle's valuation. For 48 hours, emails fly back and forth. Pinnacle is annoyed: "We don't compete on terms." They withdraw their veto clause but hold firm on liquidation preference. Blume bumps their check to ₹6.5 crore but doesn't change the valuation. You sign with Blume at the improved terms. But Pinnacle's partner tells another VC: "That founder is a tough negotiator." It's a compliment... or a warning. In startup world, reputation is everything. You got a better deal, but made a powerful enemy. Was it worth it?

choices.label: ✋ Walk Away -- Bootstrap to Profitability
choices.description: Reject both offers. You have revenue, users, and momentum. Why give up equity at all? Many great companies bootstrapped to profitability: Zoho, Zerodha, Freshworks (early years). The ultimate power move -- or the ultimate mistake.
choices.feedback: ✋ THE BOLDEST MOVE OF ALL. You reject both VCs. The startup ecosystem is SHOCKED. "They turned down ₹8 crore?!" Twitter goes wild. Some call you brilliant. Some call you stupid. You cut costs ruthlessly, focus on revenue, and reach break-even in 4 months through sheer willpower. Sridhar Vembu of Zoho tweets: "Respect. Not every company needs VC money." But your growth slows. TechNova, now flush with ₹15 crore in VC funding, scales aggressively. You kept your equity but might have lost the race. The jury is still out. Only time will tell if this was visionary or foolish.

But here's the truth: 90% of startups fail, and the lessons you learned are priceless. Every great founder has a failure story. This is yours. The question is: will you try again?

glossary_terms.definition: The simplest version of a product that can be released to test a business hypothesis with real customers. It has just enough features to attract early adopters and validate the core idea, without wasting resources on unnecessary features.
glossary_terms.example: Zomato started as a simple website that scanned and uploaded restaurant menus -- no ordering, no delivery, just menus. That was their MVP, and it proved that people wanted restaurant information online.

glossary_terms.definition: The rate at which a startup spends money each month before generating positive cash flow. It's typically measured in rupees or dollars per month. A high burn rate means the company is spending money quickly, reducing its runway.
glossary_terms.example: If your startup has ₹12 lakh in the bank and spends ₹2 lakh per month, your burn rate is ₹2 lakh/month and your runway is 6 months. After that, you're out of money unless you raise more or start earning revenue.

glossary_terms.definition: The first significant round of venture capital financing for a startup, typically ranging from ₹5 crore to ₹50 crore in India. It usually happens after the startup has proven product-market fit with early traction. Series A investors get equity (ownership percentage) in exchange for their investment.
glossary_terms.example: Razorpay raised its Series A of $9 million from Tiger Global and Matrix Partners in 2016, after proving that Indian businesses needed better payment infrastructure. Today it's valued at over $7.5 billion.

glossary_terms.definition: A fundamental change in a startup's business strategy, product, or target market based on learning from customers and the market. Pivoting doesn't mean failure -- it means the founder is smart enough to adapt when the original plan isn't working.
glossary_terms.example: Slack started as a gaming company called Tiny Speck. When their game failed, they realized the internal communication tool they built for their team was more valuable than the game itself. They pivoted to become a $27 billion company.

glossary_terms.definition: A non-binding document outlining the key terms and conditions of an investment. It includes the valuation, amount of investment, equity percentage, liquidation preferences, board seats, and other rights. It's the foundation for the final legal agreement between founder and investor.
glossary_terms.example: A term sheet might say: ₹5 crore investment at ₹25 crore pre-money valuation (16.7% equity), 1x liquidation preference, one board seat for the investor, and a 15% ESOP pool for employees. Every clause matters!
